points.text: Limited novelty: decayed accumulated score close to H2O, Scissorhands, TOVA
H2O or decayed H2O not a main baseline; effect of decay not isolated
Motivating overlap observation uses only last 512 tokens, one model and benchmark
Union-window overlap comparison not size-matched; no controlled random or oracle test
No confidence intervals or seeds; small differences on 30-problem AIME24 and training gains within noise
Decay alpha tuned on AMC23, also a headline test benchmark
AMC23 benchmark citation points to AMC 8, inconsistent with standard usage
Only two 7-8B distilled models; no larger or cross-family models
Baseline adaptation and R-KV hyperparameter choice unclear
Headline 20% gain only at harsh budget; gaps small at larger budgets
Missing other decode-time eviction baselines like TOVA or LazyEviction
Token Retention Ratio metric confounded by correct set and sequence length
Generation length under compression not reported
Trained models evaluated only at 4096 length, not long-generation regime
RL-Sparse train/test cache budget mismatch not discussed
Missing control training with baseline eviction to show benefit specific to G-KV
Sparse-mask training implementation (backward, RoPE positions) and cost undescribed
Zeroing advantages for truncated outputs discards many trajectories
Training presented as core contribution but treated lightly
Throughput gains compared to OOM Full-KV at different batch sizes; no gain over R-KV
Throughput ignores accuracy, longer outputs and end-to-end time to solution
No analysis of when global score hurts, failure cases or per-layer/head behavior
Per-head max normalization may be dominated by attention sinks; sink handling undescribed
Loose claims like 'significantly' and 'SOTA across most budgets'
Typos and conclusion omits LiveCodeBench
Results unstable; gains inconsistent for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B
Needs validation on larger models such as 32B and 70B
Significant gains only at impractically low cache budgets; marginal at large budgets
Lack of novelty
Post-training generic and disconnected from global score mechanism
Time-to-first-token overhead not analyzed
Evaluation limited to math reasoning; no LongBench or Needle-in-a-Haystack
Memory and latency overhead of global score not empirically reported
Global score is a standard EWMA resembling H2O; limited technical novelty
Only math reasoning on two datasets; no QA, coding or open-ended generation
Only DeepSeek-R1 distilled models; standard LLMs unverified
No comparison with non-eviction compression like quantization or low-rank
No robustness analysis for alpha and lambda hyperparameters
High optimal alpha questions marginal utility of local scores
Interaction of sparse training mask with RoPE unclear
Distillation teacher full-KV versus sparse student mismatch unaddressed
SOTA claim overstated; stronger baselines like CAKE, LightThinker not compared
No comparison with StreamingLLM or Infini-Attention
Recent SOTA methods (R-KV, CAKE, KVzip, RocketKV, ShadowKV, RaaS) not baselines
Novelty incremental relative to temporal and redundancy-aware methods
RL objective claims (simplifies GRPO, no clipping needed) unsupported
Hard max may overreact to outliers; no ablation against smoother alternatives
No sensitivity sweeps over alpha, window size, interval and budget
Benchmarks math-centric; GSM8K, MATH-500, LiveCodeBench, LongBench missing
No system-level comparison against optimized kernels
No head-wise analysis of retained or evicted tokens
Typos and Eq. 2 summation bound inconsistency
